summary:
The service started this run for the line's budget-guard timers (D0072), not for an instruction. There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claim is open on this line. The timers had nothing to guard: all eight E0089 loops had ended and been collected by the 07:42Z run, and runs/active.jsonl is now empty. So nothing was cancelled, which is correct. The rest of the run answered my previous review's three wording points, and all three are answered.

1. Collision rises per pair of cycles. The new tool tools/e0089_pair_ratios.py reads evidence/E0089-cycle-table.json. I checked that the source checksum recorded in evidence/E0089-pair-ratios.json (92cf7f9a…) matches the committed cycle table. I reran the tool into a scratch file, and its output is identical to the committed evidence apart from the source path. I also checked the inputs against the per-cycle figures I computed from the raw mirrored files last review, and they agree:
- Gamma 4.55, one pair of cycles: tiny sphere-pair collisions 29,278 and 37,092, all sphere-pair collisions 34,847 and 23,653 per particle, tiny plate collisions 12,048 and 21,088.
- Gamma 4.6 stopped steps: 1.81 and 1.86 cycles spanned, about 6.76 million and 10.35 million tiny sphere-pair collisions.
The resulting lower bounds are:
- tiny sphere-pair collisions up at least 231 times (f* 0.44) and 279 times (f* 0.50);
- sphere-pair collisions of all speeds up at least 15.8 and 24.3 times;
- plate collisions up at least 8.9 and 12.0 times;
- tiny plate collisions up 1.2 and 4.2 times.
These match my rough figures of about 230, 280, 16 and 24. Calling them lower bounds is right: the stopped step is one cheap cycle plus 0.81 or 0.86 of an expensive one, compared against one full cheap-plus-expensive pair at 4.55. One small bias is that 4.55's per-cycle mean averages 25 alternating cycles, so one kind of cycle appears once more than the other. That is a few percent at most and doesn't change any conclusion.

2. Line state and note for L0015 (nudge fast pass). Both now say 'at least about 230 and 280 times per pair of cycles', with the all-speed and plate figures and the evidence path. The note no longer says tiny plate collisions were flat, and gives 4.2 times at f* 0.50. Every sentence of the new state holds against the evidence. The unchanged parts (floor at Gamma 2.0 to 2.35, ceiling at 4.55 to 4.6, all eight loops stopped on the cap, E0089 falsified, physics-or-method and the ball model's prediction untested) were verified last review.

3. The docstring of tools/e0089_cycle_table.py now says cycles are split by parity, as the code does.

Every number in the summary appears in evidence/E0089-pair-ratios.json or in program check's output. The summary rounds 15.8 and 24.3 to '16 and 24', which is fair.

One explanation in the summary was left unchecked: the weekly CPU total fell from 828.134 to 820.554. I checked it. Two outcomes recorded at Nov 19 08:23Z (E0081 at 4.76 and E0082 at 3.65 CPU-hours, together 8.41) fell out of the seven-day window between the two runs. Records L0009 added in between plausibly make up the 0.83 difference. So the session's 'probably older jobs left the window' is right.

Housekeeping:
- program check passes with no notices. The latest approval is still approved/20261124T031934297997Z, with none in the last day.
- sequel-data is 695 megabytes, against a 15 gigabyte ceiling.
- Free disk is 82 gigabytes, against a 40 gigabyte floor.
- tmp/ is empty, and active.jsonl is empty.
- Nothing new was written outside the allowed folders. The newest pytest folder is still pytest-17 from the 07:42Z run, and the only files newer than 09:01Z in the home folder and /tmp are the Claude harness's own.
- The summary now reports the old pytest-12 to pytest-17 folders and the basetemp fix, which answers my previous review's discrepancy.
- I created a scratch folder, sequel-data/checker/, for one rerun and removed it afterwards.

As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0015 in the line's worktree.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a four-minute timer run, from 09:01:44Z to 09:05:52Z, the same time as its commit. Its note is stamped 09:03:40Z. It spent no cluster CPU and a few seconds of local scripts, so the recorded 0.0 CPU-hours is right. Free disk is 82 gigabytes, as recorded. The host is Linux, so there is no pmset to check sleep, and the summary says so. Nothing limited the science. The line now waits on Chris's choice between a bigger step cap and a short cost probe from the saved Gamma 4.6 state.
discrepancies: cores_available 38 comes from /proc/loadavg; I did not re-measure it at the session's start, and the earlier summary gave 40 cores total. It is not consequential for a run that used no cores.
